Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure was a game I completely forgot about over the years, only rediscovering it recently while searching for another game. Immediately, I was hit with a heavy dose of nostalgia from my childhood in the early '90s! Unfortunately, I've never managed to complete the game, but maybe one day I will. Thank you, Steam, for keeping gems like this alive!

Game Overview:
Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure, released in 1992 by Apogee Software, is a platformer that follows the adventures of Cosmo, a young alien who explores different planets to rescue his parents. The game is known for its vibrant graphics, engaging gameplay, and challenging levels that require both skill and strategy to navigate.

Gameplay:
Players control Cosmo as he jumps, climbs, and explores various levels filled with traps, puzzles, and enemies. Each level presents unique challenges and requires players to collect items and avoid dangers to progress.

Graphics and Sound:
The game features colorful and detailed pixel art typical of early '90s PC games. The soundtrack and sound effects complement the gameplay, enhancing the immersive experience of exploring alien worlds.

So, I played this game when I was a kid. My brothers, my friends and I LOVED it. Problem was, we only had the first episode. This was back in the days of 'shareware,' when you were ENCOURAGED to share a game, but then you either had to buy the remaining episodes, or unlock the game somehow, or just however it worked. So, we all played Episode 1 over and over, trying to see who could get the highest score, and never really continued our adventure.

Fast forward to modern times, when I remembered playing, wanted to play again, and found it on Steam. I bought this, full price, without thinking. And, off to the past I go.

Now, I wanted an authentic Cosmo experience, and that's exactly what I got. No re-mastered this, no re-vamped that, just DOS-level Cosmo as I played it all those years ago. And that's exactly what this is: Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure episodes 1, 2, and 3. BOOM.

Basics of the game: You play as Cosmo, a little green alien with suction cup hands. You're trying to go to Disney World with your parents. Something is wrong with the spaceship. You land on an unknown planet. You wander off. When you return, your parents are gone. Now you're going to have to... idk, go through all kinds of madness to find them again.

It's basically 30 levels, plus 'bonus' levels where you can rack up some extra points. 10 levels per episode. You will jump on platforms, bounce on springs, use suction cup arms to stick to walls, drop bombs, collect points, and all kinds of other stuff. I mean, look at the pictures. It's not hard to figure out what you'll be doing.

I also don't really need to spend a lot of time commenting on graphics, sound effects, music, and so on. This is a DOS game created decades ago. This is going to pan out exactly as you expect it to. It will have silly noises, low frame rate graphics, and repetitive songs. But that's part of the charm of old DOS games. That's how we grew up. That's where the original action was.

So, overall, great deal - back in the day, episodes 2 and 3 were... oh, I can't even remember. It says it in the game, but I'm blanking. Like 40 bucks or something. You can get the entire series for 5 bucks here, so it's a steal.

Oh... and episodes 2 and 3 were a lot harder than episode 1. So if you're like me and only played ep 1 back in the day... buckle up.

Overall definite recommend. A blast straight from the past. I thoroughly enjoyed playing this game.

Cosmo's Cosmic Adventure é um jogo que fez parte da infância de muitas pessoas. Um jogo atemporal que apesar das grandes limitações da idade é um ótimo jogo, bastante divertido e desafiador.

Conforme os episódios vão avançando o jogo fica mais difícil, ainda assim empolgante até o final. Apesar da linearidade e da história simples, o avanço dos niveis dão certa percepção de progressão pela mudança do cenários, inimigos e coletáveis. A base do jogo é o acúmulo de pontos mas ainda assim contém easter eggs e áreas secretas que dão itens para aumentar a barra de vida do personagem, facilitando um pouco o jogo.

Eu recomendo este clássico pela diversão e nostalgia, e você não terá problemas em jogar pela steam. pois o dosbox está bem configurado por padrão.
